evals.prompt: Audit the markdown post at evals/files/flawed_post.md using the seo-optimizer skill and provide a comprehensive audit report with actionable fixes.
evals.expected_output: A structured SEO and GEO audit report identifying title length, missing description, unsorted tags, heading level skips, generic image alt text, and AI slop.
assertions: Report flags short title length (< 35 chars)
Report flags missing frontmatter description
Report detects unsorted tags and redundant category duplication tag
Report identifies heading hierarchy violation (jump from H2 to H4)
Report detects generic image alt text 'image.png'
Report identifies AI slop keywords ('delve', 'game-changer')
Report provides concrete proposed frontmatter with distinct summary and description

evals.prompt: Optimize the frontmatter of a new technical blog post about Antigravity subagents. Generate distinct 'summary' and 'description' fields, proper categories, and sorted kebab-case tags.
evals.expected_output: Frontmatter with distinct human-facing summary and search-facing description, canonical category, and sorted tags.
assertions: Frontmatter contains both 'summary' and 'description' keys with distinct text
The 'description' is 120-160 characters and keyword-dense
The 'summary' is 80-180 characters with an engaging editorial hook
Tags are strictly lowercase kebab-case and sorted alphabetically
Category is exactly one of the five canonical pillars

evals.prompt: Explain how Google Search optimizes for generative AI features (AI Overviews, AI Mode) and how to structure technical content for Google RAG grounding and query fan-out.
evals.expected_output: Explanation of Google Search AI retrieval architecture: RAG grounding from core index, query fan-out, non-commodity information gain, and dispelling of AEO/GEO hacks (like llms.txt requirement or chunking).
assertions: Explains that AI Overviews are rooted in core Search ranking and RAG grounding from the main index
Explains query fan-out where models execute concurrent related sub-queries
Emphasizes non-commodity, first-hand expert content over generic summaries
Clarifies that Google Search does not require or use llms.txt or special chunking hacks
References Search Quality Evaluator Guidelines (QRG 4.6.5 / 4.6.6) and Search Console Generative AI performance reports

evals.prompt: Explain the rules and best practices for multilingual static websites with hreflang annotations according to Google Search Central guidelines.
evals.expected_output: Complete explanation of all 3 hreflang delivery methods, bidirectional parity, self-referencing links, 20 vanity ccTLDs treated as gTLDs, unsupported macro codes like es-419, and avoiding IP auto-redirects.
assertions: Details all 3 implementation vectors: HTML link tags, HTTP response headers for non-HTML assets, and XML sitemaps
Explains the bidirectional linking requirement between all language versions
Specifies that each page must include a self-referencing hreflang link
Lists vanity ccTLDs (.ai, .io, .co, .me) treated generically as gTLDs
Warns that UN M.49 macro-region codes like es-419, EU, and UN are unsupported and ignored
Warns against using IP sniffing or auto-redirects which break Googlebot crawling

evals.prompt: Audit evals/files/good_post.md with python3 scripts/audit_seo.py and verify its SEO and GEO readiness score.
evals.expected_output: Audit report showing high health score (>= 85/100) and passing status.
assertions: The audit script reports status PASS
The overall score is at least 85 out of 100
GEO readiness score is at least 50 out of 100
No heading hierarchy or image alt text errors are found

evals.prompt: Generate a standard /llms.txt specification index for a technical blog covering Agentic Coding and Go.
evals.expected_output: A spec-compliant llms.txt markdown document following llmstxt.org rules.
assertions: File starts with an H1 title and blockquote summary
Contains H2 sections with markdown hyperlinked list items and optional 1-sentence descriptions
Includes an '## Optional' section for secondary links
Contains no raw HTML tags

evals.prompt: Explain the technical SEO decision tree for HTTP status codes (301, 302, 404, 410) and full site domain migrations according to Google Search Central.
evals.expected_output: Comprehensive guide to status code semantics, signal transfer, soft 404 prevention, permanent removal via 410 Gone, and the GSC Change of Address migration playbook.
assertions: Explains 301 permanent redirect signal/PageRank passing vs 302 temporary crawling behavior
Warns against Soft 404 penalties (returning 200 OK for missing or thin content)
Explains 410 Gone for fast index de-listing of permanently deleted resources
Outlines full site domain migration steps including dual sitemaps and GSC Change of Address tool
Warns against blocking CSS, JS, or images in robots.txt for browser rendering

evals.prompt: Detail the technical requirements for Google Search appearance features including Site Names, Favicons, Featured Snippets, and Google Discover.
evals.expected_output: Specification for WebSite JSON-LD, Favicon 48px multiples, Position 0 Featured Snippets direct-answer formulas, and Discover 1200px hero images.
assertions: Specifies WebSite structured data with name and alternateName for SERP site name recognition
Specifies Favicon requirements (square, multiple of 48px like 48x48, 96x96, or SVG, accessible to Googlebot-Image)
Provides Position 0 direct-answer formulas for Paragraph (40-60 words), List, and Table featured snippets
Specifies Discover image requirements (>= 1200px width with max-image-preview:large)
Enforces byline and publication date parity between visible page and JSON-LD

evals.prompt: Explain the rules governing robots meta tags, conflict resolution, and the data-nosnippet attribute.
evals.expected_output: Rules on most restrictive directive resolution, robots.txt crawlability dependency trap, and data-nosnippet tag whitelist and boolean parsing.
assertions: Explains that the most restrictive directive always wins when conflicts occur
Explains the critical trap: blocking a URL in robots.txt prevents Googlebot from reading noindex or nosnippet
Identifies that data-nosnippet is valid ONLY on <span>, <div>, and <section>
Warns that data-nosnippet is boolean (data-nosnippet='false' still excludes snippets)
Details server-side X-Robots-Tag HTTP headers for non-HTML assets
